$comment: The shape of the private denied-term list that bin/lib/release-terms.mjs reads from the sidecar (monitor/release-terms.json) or from CW_RELEASE_TERMS. The list is a detector derived from the publication boundary's ownership table: every term declares the key its reports are labelled by, why it is denied and the test a reader applies to a hit; a term whose pattern is too wide is narrowed by an exception naming one exact path and the count measured there, rather than dropped; and a term withdrawn keeps the measurement that withdrew it. The real list names private things; every term here is synthetic.

rules.why: a tool that is not part of the product

words.why: the tool is a dependency of the maintainer's workflow, not a feature of the product
words.test: does the text name the tool, or the capability and its contract? a capability survives publication under its own name

words.why: a service of the maintainer's that this product calls over a CW_* configured address
words.test: replace the name with the interface it implements; if the sentence still says what the code does, the name was disclosure
words.measured: 2026-01-01: 2 hits in docs/example-interface.md, 1 of them the declared heading where the name is the subject of a reviewed public description. The count withdraws that one; a second occurrence in the same file is reported, so the exception is an allowance and not a blind file.

rules.why: a pseudonym that stands in for a customer

patterns.why: the pseudonym indexes the reversal table the sidecar holds, so publishing it publishes half the mapping
patterns.test: is the letter drawn from the engagement roster? a synthetic fixture uses example-customer-x or -y, which this pattern does not match

rules.why: a ruling or an incident from the maintainer's own history

patterns.why: a ruling is a record of the maintainer deciding, which no reader of the public tree can check
patterns.test: can a reader of the public tree verify the claim from the public tree? a ruling is verifiable only against the private register

patterns.why: a dated incident is an operational record of the maintainer's own fleet
patterns.test: is the date attached to something that happened on the maintainer's machines, or to a published contract a consumer depends on?

removed.why: a publicly released third-party model family, in the same category as four other model names the list does not deny
removed.measured: 2026-01-01: 12 of 12 hits were a model identifier passed through CW_LLM_MODEL; the tree carries four further undenied model names, so the rule fired on one member of a category
